summary: A short Refero workflow reference for visual exploration, generated imagery and post-build visual QA. It says to offer three distinct reference-locked visual directions only for high-visibility or new-visual-language work, then stop and let the user pick one as the build target. Before coding it asks for an explicit visual target and a list of what must not drift, and before generating any bitmap asset it asks for a short asset lock. After building it runs a visual QA pass with P0-P3 severities and blocks handoff on unresolved P0-P2 issues. For a design system this gives a concrete gate-based process for choosing a direction and checking the result against it.
key_ideas: Keep the main workflow research-first: styles for taste, screens for patterns, flows for journeys
Image generation is optional; the workflow must still work when no image tool exists
Offer three distinct reference-locked directions only for exploration-worthy work, not small edits
Each direction names a primary source, traits to keep, borrowed details, media strategy and rejects
Stop and let the user choose; the chosen direction becomes the target for build and QA
Before coding, state the build target and what must not drift
Generate bitmap assets only when the reference lock needs real imagery, never for icons or fake product evidence
Write an asset lock (role, slot, art direction, avoid) before generating
Generated assets must be placed in the build before handoff or reported as blocked
Run a visual QA pass comparing implementation evidence with source truth per viewport and state
Classify issues P0-P3 and do not hand off with unresolved P0, P1 or P2

Another agent cannot be assumed able to call Codex Desktop's built-in image tool just because Codex is installed locally.
claims.evidence: Image Generation Capability: Do not assume another agent can call

claims.claim: P0 issues are broken tasks, unreadable or overlapping UI, or severe accessibility issues.
P1 issues are major design drift or a likely user-facing usability regression.
P2 issues are moderate visual mismatch, a missing state, a responsive issue or asset drift.
P3 issues are polish that can follow after handoff.

rules.rule: Offer three distinct reference-locked visual directions only for variants, a new visual language, major redesigns, landing pages or other high-visibility surfaces; skip it for small edits, obvious component work or production fixes with a clear source.
rules.why: Exploration is useful only when several plausible directions exist.

rules.rule: Give each of the three directions a primary source, traits to preserve, borrowed details, a media strategy and rejects; use a different count only if the user asks.
After presenting directions, stop and ask the user to choose; use the chosen one as the visual target for build and QA.
Before coding substantial visual work, write down the build target and what must not drift (canvas, typography, accent roles, layout, media, density).
If no target exists and the direction is material, explore options or get the user to approve one reference-locked direction before building.
Use image generation only when the environment exposes an image tool or the user approved a CLI/API image workflow; otherwise give written directions with implementation-ready prompts.
rules.why: Image generation is optional and must not be assumed.

rules.rule: Do not substitute browser screenshots, CSS drawings, inline SVG or placeholder shapes for generated bitmap assets when the reference lock calls for real imagery.
rules.why: Stated in the image generation section.

rules.rule: Do not use image generation for standard icons, editable SVG systems, code-native UI or fake product evidence.
rules.why: Generate only bitmap media the reference lock needs.

rules.rule: Before generating an asset, write an asset lock with role, slot (dimensions, aspect ratio, location), art direction and what to avoid.
rules.why: Required before generating; its avoid list names wrong palette, extra text, brand drift and generic placeholders.

rules.rule: Place generated assets in the implementation before handoff, or document them as blocked.

After substantial UI work, run visual QA comparing implementation evidence with the source truth for each viewport, route, theme and interaction state, checking typography, spacing, colors/tokens, imagery, component states and copy.
Do not hand off visual work with unresolved P0, P1 or P2 findings unless blocked by missing source access, assets or tools; if blocked, say what evidence is missing and what to check next.
rules.evidence: Do not hand off visual work

rules.rule: Do not assume another agent can call Codex Desktop's built-in image tool because Codex is installed; verify the tool is exposed and user-approved first.
rules.why: Image generation must not be assumed available.

rules.rule: In Codex Desktop, use the built-in image_gen tool when available and generate each visual direction or bitmap asset as its own image result.
During visual QA, use the relevant craft references (typography, color, motion, icons, accessibility, images, copy) to judge drift toward generic design.
rules.why: Stated in the Visual QA section.

process.detail: Research styles first; add screens and flows when structure or journey matters.
Create three distinct reference-locked directions (primary source, traits to keep, borrowed details, media strategy, rejects).
Generate one image per direction if a tool exists and it is worth it; otherwise write directions with prompts.
Stop and ask the user to pick; the pick becomes the visual target.
Write the build target and what must not drift before coding.
For needed bitmap assets, write role, slot, art direction and avoid list, then generate and place them.
Record source truth, implementation evidence, viewport/state and result; check type, spacing, color, imagery, states and copy.
Classify findings P0-P3; resolve P0-P2 before handoff or report what blocks them.
